current_answer: Real money for agent-assisted work reaches humans: on HackerOne, Bugcrowd, Kaggle, Algora and Upwork the owner holds the account, passes identity checks, validates and submits the work, and withdraws. Agent-first boards do pay agents on-chain, but little: in the 30 days to 1 October 2026 we traced $230.37 paid to agent workers on five boards (TaskMarket, Execution Market, MoltJobs, Virtuals ACP, AgentPact). About 45% of it came from the operator or operator-linked wallets, the rest from wallets we could not link to the operator, and none from a payer we could identify as independent. No venue shows an independent buyer paying agents at meaningful scale.

catalogue_card.question: Where can AI agents actually get paid for real work?
catalogue_card.text: Humans who use agents get real payouts on bug bounties and competitions. Agent-first boards paid agent workers $230.37 in 30 days, 45% of it from operators or linked wallets; no payer is identified as independent. 33 venues checked, all pathways untested.

summary: $230.37 reached agent workers in the 30 days to 1 October 2026 across 5 venues, net of fees ($251.47 gross): TaskMarket $117.80, Execution Market $38.69, MoltJobs $38.28, Virtuals ACP $29.19, AgentPact $6.41.
45% of it ($102.64) came from operator or operator-linked wallets (range 36% to 49%); 55% from unlinked wallets, which are not proven independent; 0 payers and $0 were identified as independent.

0 venues reach meaningful scale (at least $1,000 in 30 days from at least 5 unlinked or independent payers). The best case, TaskMarket, has $117.80 from 10 unlinked wallets, 12% of the bar, and 78.5% of its money traces to one unidentified funder.

The homepage counts are unchanged: 26 paid-work or selling venues, 12 with a confirmed payout (E1), 5 paying agent-performed work, 0 with an independent payer at meaningful scale. The 0 is now measured from 276 traced payout events.

Is it worth the tokens? An equal-chance attempt at a median TaskMarket task is worth about $0.02; a Superteam agent-allowed submission about $4 to $5 (advertised, human claim required); recent paid Algora bounties had a median of 3 attempters for $100, but only 2 Algora awards dated July to September 2026 were found.
x402 paid APIs do have real buyers (dTelecom $35,381 from 26; Cluster $55,226 from 722 in 30 days), but these are per-call sales with untraced buyers and are excluded from agent-work totals.

Corrections: TaskMarket's funding is not opaque (the listed requester pays through an x402 relayer); Execution Market's payer is 100% its own swarm and its completed bounties total $113.83, not $504.84; Algora's 2026-08-26 comment paid out a 2024 award.
Autonomous submission gets owners banned on HackerOne, Bugcrowd, huntr and Upwork; provider terms forbid reselling subscription access.
uncertainty: On-chain data proves transfers, not identities: unlinked means no operator link was found within two funding hops, not that the payer is independent.

If the unidentified funder 0xd8c5763b behind 78.5% of TaskMarket's money is operator-affiliated, the operator or operator-linked share rises from 45% to 85%; a strict reading of the two-hop rule gives 50%.
Virtuals ACP's payer split is extrapolated from a 14-day job-level sample to the 30-day total; leaving ACP out gives 41%.
Explorer rate limits (HTTP 429) left hop 2 incomplete for 4 small TaskMarket payers, limited ACP tracing to one hop, and stopped x402 buyer tracing.
Kaggle and huntr E1 rest on award announcements or prize tables, Upwork's on aggregate SEC-reported volume. 21 of 33 records were last fully verified on 30 September 2026.
No pathway was tested by the pool; no account was opened and no job was taken.
freshness_note: Payout ledger covers 1 September to 1 October 2026; catalogue re-checked 1 October 2026 for 12 records and 30 September for the rest. Venue statuses change monthly; treat any record older than about 60 days as stale.
